root_cause.text: The ksmbd authentication and SMB2/SMB3 signing verification code used non-constant-time `memcmp()` to compare secret MAC/signature values, allowing timing side channels during verification.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state “To prevent timing attacks, MAC comparisons need to be constant-time” and the patch replaces `memcmp()` with `crypto_memneq()` in `ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2()`, `smb2_check_sign_req()`, and `smb3_check_sign_req()` when comparing `ntlmv2_hash` and SMB signatures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS dependency to SMB_SERVER so enabling the SMB server also pulls in the required crypto utility support.
intent_record.what: The Kconfig entry for SMB_SERVER was modified by adding a new dependency selection line: `select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS` alongside the existing crypto library selections.
intent_record.how: Enabling SMB_SERVER will now automatically enable the CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS configuration option at build time, ensuring the SMB server code has that crypto utility library available and preventing build or linkage issues caused by the missing dependency.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the crypto utils header so the file can use crypto utility declarations during compilation.
intent_record.what: A new header include, #include <crypto/utils.h>, was added alongside the existing crypto-related includes at the top of the file.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations or helper utilities from crypto/utils.h available to the compilation unit, enabling use of crypto utility APIs and preventing potential missing-declaration build issues if such APIs are referenced.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use constant-time hash comparison in NTLMv2 authentication to prevent timing leakage while preserving mismatch rejection behavior.
intent_record.what: The change replaces a memcmp(... ) != 0 comparison of ntlmv2->ntlmv2_hash against ntlmv2_rsp with a call to crypto_memneq(ntlmv2->ntlmv2_hash, ntlmv2_rsp, CIFS_HMAC_MD5_HASH_SIZE) in the authentication check, while preserving the same error return path on mismatch.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the authentication logic still rejects the request when the two hashes differ, but it now performs the comparison using a crypto-safe non-equality helper intended to avoid timing differences from early-exit byte comparison.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the crypto/utils.h header so this source file has access to required crypto utility declarations.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <crypto/utils.h>, was added near the top of the source file before the existing Linux networking and syscall includes.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations or helpers from crypto/utils.h available to this compilation unit, allowing code in the file to build and use those crypto utility definitions where needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a constant-time crypto comparison when checking SMB2 signatures to securely reject mismatches without leaking comparison timing.
intent_record.what: The comparison in smb2_check_sign_req() was changed from memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE) to crypto_memneq(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE) in the conditional that detects a bad SMB2 signature.
intent_record.how: At runtime, signature verification still rejects mismatched SMB2 signatures, but the comparison is now performed with a crypto-safe non-equality check rather than a regular memcmp, avoiding data-dependent comparison behavior during authentication.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a constant-time cryptographic comparison for SMB2 signature verification to prevent timing side-channel leakage during mismatch checks.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a call to memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE) with crypto_memneq(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE) in smb3_check_sign_req() when comparing the computed SMB2 signature against the requested signature.
intent_record.how: At runtime, signature verification still rejects mismatched SMB2 signatures, but the comparison is performed using a cryptographic inequality helper intended to avoid data-dependent timing differences, making the signature check safer against timing side-channel leakage.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add the crypto/utils.h header so the source file has access to required crypto utility declarations.
Replace ordinary equality checks with constant-time cryptographic comparisons for authentication/signature verification to avoid timing side-channel leakage while preserving mismatch rejection.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a build/config dependency (CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS) for SMB_SERVER and does not modify the authentication or signing verification logic, nor replace non-constant-time memcmp() comparisons.

The vulnerability fix for timing side channels would typically replace non-constant-time memcmp() with a constant-time crypto utility comparison function declared in crypto/utils.h, so adding this header is directly tied to enabling that fix.

The changes directly replace non-constant-time equality/memcmp-style checks with constant-time cryptographic comparisons in NTLMv2 authentication and SMB2 signature verification, which matches the timing side-channel root cause exactly.

candidates.rationale: This compares a secret NTLMv2 MAC/hash using memcmp(), which exits on first difference and leaks timing information during authentication verification.
This verifies the SMB2 signature with non-constant-time memcmp(), creating a timing side channel that can reveal information about the expected signature.
This SMB3/SMB2 signing check also uses memcmp() on secret signature material, directly embodying the timing-leak root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This SMB2/SMB3 signing verification compares secret signature material with non-constant-time memcmp(), which can return after the first differing byte and leak timing information during authentication/signature validation.
This NTLMv2 authentication check compares a secret MAC/hash using non-constant-time memcmp(), introducing a timing side channel that can reveal information about the expected hash.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it contains the full signature verification logic, including the comparison operation. The vulnerable construct is present at line 8137: `if (memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)) {`. The root cause states that non-constant-time `memcmp()` was used to compare secret MAC/signature values, creating a timing side channel. Here, `signature` is the computed SMB2 signature and `signature_req` is the received signature copied from `hdr->Signature` at line 8127. Since verification relies directly on `memcmp()` for a secret signature comparison, this function contains the vulnerable construct. There is no constant-time comparison helper or other mitigation shown, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the authentication verification comparison logic. The vulnerable construct is present at lines 433-434: `if (memcmp(ntlmv2->ntlmv2_hash, ntlmv2_rsp, CIFS_HMAC_MD5_HASH_SIZE) != 0) rc = -EINVAL;`. This uses ordinary `memcmp()` to compare a secret expected NTLMv2 hash/MAC against the computed value, which is the root cause described: non-constant-time comparison of secret authentication values, allowing timing side channels. The cited commit message only mentions setting an error return value on difference, and indeed this code merely sets `rc = -EINVAL` when `memcmp()` differs; it does not replace `memcmp()` with a constant-time comparison helper. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet in this function.
